opener.caption: Ein Hinterhof in Berlin, am Morgen. Wer sitzt hier am Abend?
reading.intro: Maya has lived in the building for some months. Frau Huber lives on the first floor, right above the courtyard. This morning she is at her window, as always, and Maya is taking out the rubbish.
reading.photos[0].caption: Der Hof: Fahrräder, Bäume, und vierzig Fenster sehen alles.
reading.photos[1].caption: Eine Mülltonne in Berlin: Krassere Öffnungszeiten als dein Späti!
reading.en: Frau Huber: Good morning, Frau Maya! You're getting up late today. · Maya: Good morning, Frau Huber. It's only half past eight. · Frau Huber: Usually you get up at eight. At quarter past eight you turn on the light in the kitchen. · Maya: You know that? · Frau Huber: My window looks onto the courtyard. Herr Yilmaz gets up at four, he's a baker. Lena comes back at seven, she works nights. · Maya: And the young man in the attic? · Frau Huber: He calls his mother every evening at six. She cries, he cries. · Maya: And me? · Frau Huber: You do your shopping on Saturdays, always at five to eight. In the evening you watch TV. At eleven you turn the light off. Then you turn it on again and eat chocolate. · Maya: Frau Huber! And you? What do you do all day? Do you watch TV too? · Frau Huber: Me? No. I don't watch TV. I open the window.
reading.fact: Berlin's old blocks were built in layers, courtyard behind courtyard. The front house was for the well-off, the back for the workers. Today the *Hinterhof* flat is the quiet one, and the bins are the village square.

document.caption: Öffnungszeiten: Wann macht das Jugendzentrum auf?
document.intro: A real sign on a youth centre. *Öffnungszeiten* are opening hours, and you will read them on every door in Germany. *Geschlossen* means closed. *14.00 – 21.00* is written with a full stop, not a colon.
document.fact: In German you can say *Das Café macht um acht auf* and *Das Café öffnet um acht*: the first splits, the second doesn’t. Same café.
